title: Line spacing set on a font with built-in leading comes out as asked
goal: Setting a title or text line spacing tighter than normal does nothing like what was asked on fonts that carry their own extra line gap (DIN Condensed among them): at 80% the lines sit as far apart as at 100%. Make line spacing mean the same distance between lines on every font.
notes: Reproduced 2026-11-21 in task keynote-clean-soft-gradient-glass-kinetic-bold-t. A probe test printed for Condensed Poster (DIN Condensed, 360 pt, lineHeight 0.8, "YOUR\nTITLE"): frame height 726, and CTFontGetAscent/Descent/Leading = 256.3 / 103.7 / 72.0. Measuring the rendered hold frame (PHOTONZ_REEL=1 ... --filter TitleRedesignReel, after/hold-kinetic.png) the two lines of capitals had ink rows (130,386) and (488,748): a pitch of 358, not 288. Cause, as read: TextRasterizer.paragraphStyle sets minimumLineHeight = maximumLineHeight = lineHeight * size, and CoreText adds the font own leading on top of that, so every line is a leading taller than asked; naturalSize then measures the same. The inspector Leading control is the same number, so a person sees it too. Fix in Sources/PhotonzRender/TextRasterizer.swift (paragraphStyle, naturalSize, lineOverhang), e.g. a negative lineSpacing of the leading or a font with leading stripped; mind TextBreaksAtEveryScaleTests, MaskRevealTightLeadingTests and the calm set transcriptions.
acceptance: Two lines of DIN Condensed Bold at 360 pt with line spacing 80% sit 288 pt apart baseline to baseline (today 358 to 360)
A font with no built-in leading (SF Pro) lays out exactly as it does today, pinned by a test

Every built-in title page that sets a line spacing still passes its walks and looks as it does, or is retuned in the same change (Condensed Poster sets 0.62 to work around this and would then need 0.8)
